stories.headline: Waymo reveals its first custom chip: a 5nm TSMC ASIC running in every robotaxi

key_facts.fact: In an August 20 blog post, Waymo disclosed for the first time the architecture of its onboard computer, including a custom 5-nanometer ASIC of its own design.
key_facts.excerpt: A blog post on Thursday set out the architecture of its onboard computer, introduced a custom 5-nanometer chip of its own design, and named the seven suppliers it builds the system with.

key_facts.fact: Waymo says the ASICs alone deliver over 1,000 TOPS of machine-learning performance dedicated to front-end sensor processing.
key_facts.excerpt: The chip's dedicated front-end processing provides 1,000 TOPS (trillion operations a second).

key_facts.fact: The chip is built on TSMC's 5nm process; each autonomous driving module carries two of them, running the same workloads in parallel so one can take over if the other faults.
key_facts.excerpt: Waymo makes its ASICs using Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co.'s five-nanometer node... Waymo included two ASICs in its autonomous driving module to mitigate the impact of hardware failures. If one of the processors goes offline, the other can take over.

key_facts.fact: Waymo previously used Intel FPGAs for sensor processing; the chip's design incorporates more than 200 million miles of autonomous driving data.
key_facts.excerpt: Prior to this, Waymo had employed Intel FPGAs for sensor processing... According to Waymo, the chip's design incorporates more than 200 million miles worth of autonomous driving data.

key_facts.fact: Waymo said the in-house chip diversifies its supply beyond third parties such as Nvidia, but it still names AMD, Micron, Nvidia, Samsung, SanDisk, Socionext and TSMC as suppliers.
key_facts.excerpt: Alphabet Inc.'s Waymo has built a custom chip that the company said will improve the performance of its robotaxis, while also diversifying its chip supply beyond third-party companies such as Nvidia Corp.

key_facts.fact: Waymo says the ASIC is 'just one of several exciting custom components we're developing'.
key_facts.excerpt: Waymo also says the ASIC is "just one of several exciting custom components we're developing". More in-house silicon is coming, and the company has not said what.

stories.headline: Broadcom seeks over $60B in debt for an AI chip deal benefiting Anthropic

key_facts.fact: Bloomberg reported on Thursday, August 20, that Broadcom is in talks with lenders to raise more than $60 billion in debt for an AI chip financing deal benefiting Anthropic and other companies.
key_facts.excerpt: Broadcom is in talks with a group of lenders to raise more than $60 billion in debt for an AI chip financing deal that will benefit Anthropic and other companies, Bloomberg News reported on Thursday.

key_facts.fact: The package could include a roughly $30 billion junior tranche plus a senior-secured tranche of about $60-70 billion that Broadcom would partly guarantee, taking the total to as much as $100 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: The financing could include a roughly $30 billion junior debt tranche, while the chip designer would guarantee a part of a senior-secured tranche that could range from about $60 billion to $70 billion... The numbers under discussion would potentially bring the total raise to as much as $100 billion.

key_facts.fact: Blackstone and Apollo Global Management are in talks to participate; the debt would be issued by a special-purpose vehicle.
key_facts.excerpt: Blackstone and Apollo Global Management are in talks with Broadcom to participate in the financing... The new debt would be issued by a special-purpose vehicle and could be similar to the $35 billion agreement.

key_facts.fact: It follows a June partnership between Broadcom, Apollo and Blackstone that financed a $35 billion expansion of Anthropic's computing capacity using Broadcom custom chips, aiming at more than 20 gigawatts of compute for leading AI labs by 2028.
key_facts.excerpt: The initial commitment was expected to add one gigawatt of computing capacity, while the partnership overall aims to enable more than 20 gigawatts of compute power for leading AI labs by 2028.

key_facts.fact: Broadcom designs custom chips for Alphabet and Meta and has chip supply deals with Anthropic and OpenAI.
key_facts.excerpt: Broadcom plays a crucial role in helping design custom chips for firms like Alphabet and Meta... Broadcom also has chip supply deals with Anthropic and OpenAI.

stories.headline: Nvidia opens talks with Korean AI chip startup Rebellions; Huang met its CEO this week

key_facts.fact: Bloomberg reported on August 21 that Nvidia is in early discussions with Korean AI chip designer Rebellions about a technical partnership, an investment or even an acquisition.
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia Corp is in early discussions with the Korean artificial intelligence (AI) chip designer Rebellions about possible collaborations, including a technical partnership, an investment or perhaps even an acquisition, according to people familiar with the matter.

key_facts.fact: Jensen Huang met Rebellions co-founder and CEO Sunghyun Park at Nvidia's Santa Clara headquarters this week to discuss a tie-up.
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia chief executive officer Jensen Huang met with Rebellions co-founder and CEO Sunghyun Park and discussed a potential tie-up at the US company's headquarters in Santa Clara, California this week.

key_facts.fact: Rebellions, founded in 2020 and based in Bundang, has raised about $850 million from backers including SK hynix, Samsung Ventures and Arm, and was last valued near $2.3 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: Bundang, South Korea-based Rebellions has raised roughly US$850 million from investors including SK Hynix Inc, Samsung Ventures and Arm Holdings plc, and was most recently valued at around US$2.3 billion.

key_facts.fact: Rebellions builds neural processing units for data-center AI inference and is preparing a Korean IPO in the first half of 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: Its chips have already been deployed in commercial applications in South Korea, while the company has been expanding abroad and preparing for a potential Korean IPO in the first half of 2027.

key_facts.fact: South Korea's National Growth Fund made a 250 billion won ($166 million) direct investment in Rebellions in March, the first under the government's 'K-Nvidia' initiative.
key_facts.excerpt: The decision was made at a fund management committee meeting for the state-led 'National Growth Fund,' marking the first direct investment under the country's 'K-Nvidia' initiative.

key_facts.fact: Talks are preliminary and may not lead to a transaction; Nvidia did not respond to requests for comment and Rebellions declined to comment.
key_facts.excerpt: Deliberations between Nvidia and six-year-old Rebellions are preliminary and may not lead to a transaction, the people said.

stories.headline: Samsung approves up to $79.5B in 2026 shareholder returns, a Korean record

key_facts.fact: Samsung's board approved on Friday a 2026 shareholder return plan estimated at 90 trillion to 110 trillion won ($65.1 billion to $79.5 billion), which the company called the largest ever by a Korean company.
key_facts.excerpt: Samsung Electronics' Board of Directors convened today and approved a shareholder return plan for 2026, estimated at approximately KRW 90 trillion to KRW 110 trillion... the largest ever by a Korean company.

key_facts.fact: The package is about five times Samsung's previous annual record of 20.3 trillion won, set in 2020.
key_facts.excerpt: Shareholder return expected to be five times the Company's previous high of KRW 20.3 trillion, set in 2020.

key_facts.fact: Samsung plans roughly 30 trillion won in cash dividends in the third quarter of 2026 and approved a separate buyback of about 15 trillion won of its own shares for employee compensation.
key_facts.excerpt: Plans to distribute approximately KRW 30 trillion in dividends, including regular payouts in Q3 2026. A buy back of approximately KRW 15 trillion in shares for employee compensation planned.

key_facts.fact: The remaining returns will be decided at a January 2027 board meeting once 2026 results are final; the plan delivers on Samsung's pledge to return 50% of free cash flow over 2024-2026.
key_facts.excerpt: Samsung said it will decide the size and details of the remaining shareholder returns at a board meeting in late January 2027... under which the company pledged to return 50% of free cash flow generated between 2024 and 2026.

key_facts.fact: The announcement came days after SK hynix unveiled a 40 trillion won share buyback and cancellation plan, amid an AI-driven memory chip supercycle.
key_facts.excerpt: Local rival SK Hynix on Wednesday unveiled a 40 trillion won share buyback and cancellation plan, the largest shareholder return programme announced by a publicly listed South Korean company.

stories.headline: China's YMTC clears the way for a $4.9B Shanghai STAR Market listing

key_facts.fact: Filings on Friday showed that Yangtze Memory Technologies' application to list in Shanghai has been accepted by the exchange.
key_facts.excerpt: Chinese chipmaker Yangtze Memory Technologies Corp's (YMTC) application to list its shares in Shanghai has been accepted by the financial hub's stock exchange, filings showed on Friday.

key_facts.fact: The plan sets up a 33 billion yuan ($4.91 billion) share sale on the STAR Market, which would rank among the market's biggest-ever offerings.
key_facts.excerpt: The move sets the stage for a 33 billion yuan ($4.9 billion) share sale on Shanghai's Nasdaq-style STAR Market, that would rank among the market's biggest-ever offerings, the exchange said.

key_facts.fact: YMTC completed its pre-IPO tutoring on August 20, advised by CITIC Securities and China Securities, after filing the tutoring report in May.
key_facts.excerpt: The company, advised by CITIC Securities and China Securities Co Ltd, completed the coaching process after filing its IPO coaching report in May.

key_facts.fact: The state-backed flash memory maker's valuation could reach at least 1 trillion yuan ($148 billion), fueled by the AI-driven memory shortage and record domestic tech debuts.
key_facts.excerpt: The advancement of the state-backed chipmaking champion comes as a global AI-driven memory-chip shortage and recent record-breaking market debuts by domestic technology peers have pushed up expectations for its valuation, which could potentially reach at least 1 trillion yuan ($148 billion).

stories.headline: Nvidia denies report it will ship a China-tailored LPU inference chip by year-end

key_facts.fact: The Information reported on Thursday, citing two Nvidia employees, that the company planned small-batch shipments of an AI chip designed for Chinese customers by the end of 2026, with several customers already having placed orders.
key_facts.excerpt: The Information reported, citing two Nvidia employees, that the company planned to begin small-batch shipments of an artificial intelligence chip designed for Chinese customers by the end of the year and that several customers had already placed orders.

key_facts.fact: Nvidia publicly rejected the report the same day: 'We have no LPU sales in the China market today, and no China-specific LPU product in our roadmap.'
key_facts.excerpt: "The reporting in The Information on Nvidia's LPU is incorrect. We have no LPU sales in the China market today, and no China-specific LPU product in our roadmap," an Nvidia spokesperson said.

key_facts.fact: The chip described is a version of Nvidia's Language Processing Unit, built with technology licensed from Groq, that works alongside GPUs to speed up AI chatbot responses and complies with US export controls.
key_facts.excerpt: the chip was a version of Nvidia's LPU, a processor developed using technology licensed from startup Groq that works alongside graphics processing units (GPUs) to speed up AI chatbot responses.

key_facts.fact: Engineers reportedly modified the LPU's software to pair with processors available in China because the next-generation Vera Rubin architecture cannot be exported there under US rules.
key_facts.excerpt: The adapted LPU was reworked so the compliant hardware can pair with processors accessible in China, because Nvidia's next-generation Vera Rubin architecture cannot be exported under U.S. rules.

key_facts.fact: The report also said Nvidia is scaling shipments of its cleared H200 processors, with packaging partner Amkor finishing over one million units in the second quarter.
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia is scaling shipments of its cleared H200 processors, according to the report, with packaging partner Amkor Technology finishing over one million units in the second quarter.

key_facts.fact: Washington approved H200 sales in May to a limited group of Chinese firms including Alibaba, Tencent and ByteDance, though deliveries only recently began.
key_facts.excerpt: Washington in May approved sales of the company's H200 AI chips to a limited group of Chinese firms, including Alibaba, Tencent and ByteDance, though deliveries only recently began.

stories.headline: Supermicro board probe finds no sign management knew of $2.5B Nvidia chip smuggling

key_facts.fact: Super Micro said on Thursday that a board-led independent investigation found no evidence current senior management knew about an alleged scheme to smuggle $2.5 billion in hardware packed with Nvidia chips to China.
key_facts.excerpt: Super Micro Computer said on Thursday that an independent investigation led by its board found no evidence that current members of senior management knew about an alleged scheme to smuggle $2.5 billion in hardware packed with Nvidia chips to China.

key_facts.fact: The probe was led by lead independent director Scott Angel, a former Deloitte audit partner, and audit chair Tally Liu, with Munger, Tolles & Olson as outside counsel and AlixPartners as forensic accountants.
key_facts.excerpt: The internal probe was led by lead independent director Scott Angel, a former audit partner with Deloitte, and audit committee chair Tally Liu. They retained Munger, Tolles, & Olson as outside counsel and brought in advisory firm AlixPartners as a forensic accounting consultant.

key_facts.fact: The investigation also found no evidence the company sold export-controlled products to banned companies or individuals, and no evidence its prior financial statements were unreliable.
key_facts.excerpt: It found no evidence management knew about the alleged smuggling, no evidence the company sold export-controlled products to banned companies or individuals, and no evidence the previously issued financial statements were unreliable.

key_facts.fact: The probe followed the DOJ's March indictment of co-founder Yih-Shyan 'Wally' Liaw, a sales manager and a contractor for routing US servers through Taiwan and Southeast Asia into China; Supermicro itself was not a defendant.
key_facts.excerpt: The U.S. Justice Department last month charged co-founder Yih-Shyan Liaw, sales manager Ruei-Tsang Chang and contractor Ting-Wei Sun with allegedly running a scheme to route U.S.-made servers through Taiwan to Southeast Asia... Super Micro, which was not named as a defendant in the case, had placed Liaw and Chang on leave.

key_facts.fact: Questions remain: four Supermicro employees were detained for questioning in Taiwan last month and the company received a federal grand jury subpoena in New York in June.
key_facts.excerpt: a parallel probe by authorities in Taiwan led to four Supermicro employees being detained for questioning last month in connection with Supermicro sales to a tech company, and in June Supermicro got hit with a federal grand jury subpoena in New York.
